pr_title: Back off on generating noise in the event of a PING frame
pr_body:
If either endpoint issues a PING frame while we are introducing noise into the communication then there is a danger that the connection itself will fail. We detect the PING and then back off on generating noise for a short while. It should be sufficient to just ensure that the next datagram does not get dropped for each endpoint.

Fixes #22199
pr_comments:
Wouldn't this be a legitimate failure condition?
Not a likely one, but one we ought to cope with?

> Wouldn't this be a legitimate failure condition?
Not a likely one, but one we ought to cope with?

We do cope with failure in the sense that the if one endpoint has issued PING and doesn't get a response then it will eventually cause the connection to fail (after suitable timeouts and possible re-PINGs). But our test assumes that we can cope with noise and that this isn't visible to the application. Things just keep working - so we don't actually want to introduce so much noise into the test that the connection fails.

This is the cause of the various #22199 failures. We've introduced *too* much noise that the connection has actually failed. This PR seeks to avoid that.
Fixup pushed addressing the feedback. Also rebased to address a conflict with master.
This pull request is ready to merge
